$comment: Static transitive dependency manifest. Built by grepping the actual generalized skill files for real cross-references (process/skills/*/SKILL.md), not from memory of the source repo. 'hard' means the skill's own documented steps invoke the target and have no stated fallback; 'soft' means the skill explicitly states a fallback ('if X isn't installed, do Y yourself') or the reference is a pipeline-stage pointer to a genuinely optional next step. All hard skill-to-agent edges are satisfied automatically for any adopter who installs process/ as the integrated shelf intends, since code-reviewer and docs-writer ship as part of that same shelf - they only matter if a component is cherry-picked out of process/ on its own.

backlog.notes: ship is a conditional pipeline pointer: Step 7 dispatches archive-and-commit to /ship instead, but only for a tool with its own deploy target - most BACKLOG.md items have none, so backlog's own archive-and-commit path stays fully functional without ship installed.

spec.notes: Renamed from design-gate 2026-09-05 (two-axis SDLC redesign). Implementation (former Step 4) and the QA gate (former Step 5) moved out to their own skills, build and verify - spec no longer depends on code-reviewer directly at all, only on docs-writer for Step 6's docs-sync delegation. execution-gate is no longer a spec-stage dependency of any kind: /build now runs it automatically as its own opening gate, not an optional call spec's Step 3.5 merely recommends considering - see build's own entry for that edge. Step 0.5's scoping-inventory pointer was re-pointed 2026-09-06 (next-command-contract redesign) from initiate directly to adopt, the skill initiate itself now hands off to for that case - both are named in the step's own text (adopt as the owner, initiate as the skill that detects and routes there), so both are soft edges. initiate/adopt/build/implement-queue/backlog are pipeline-stage pointers to next-phase skills spec's own steps mention, not skills spec invokes itself.

initiate.notes: handoff is hard: Step 1.1 invokes its incoming-mode scan unconditionally, no stated fallback. backlog is hard for a different reason - bucket A's last rank is an unblocked BACKLOG.md item, handed off to backlog List mode, and the report's own closing line always names backlog as the alternative regardless of which bucket-A item ranks first. adopt/spec/implement-queue are soft: offered conditionally (the no-process-history case hands off to adopt entirely, per the 2026-09-06 next-command-contract redesign that moved the scoping-inventory body out of this skill; a queued design goes to spec; a non-empty checklist to implement-queue), never invoked unconditionally.

adopt.notes: Added 2026-09-06 (next-command-contract redesign), split out of initiate's former Step 3. Step 2 names /spec as the recommendation for the freshly-scoped area and /backlog as the named alternative if nothing's ready to design yet - both pipeline-stage pointers, never invoked directly by this skill itself.

end-task.notes: Added 2026-09-06 (next-command-contract redesign), absorbing commit and wrap-up-session as internal depth modes - one implementation of the shared git-survey logic instead of three cross-referencing copies. docs-writer is hard for the same reason wrap-up-session's own entry had it: Step 6's docs pass delegates substantial NOTES.md/rules-doc writes to it. handoff is soft: Step 4's routing table names it in every row as the alternative (or the recommendation, when work is unfinished), but never invokes it unconditionally - the whole point of the rewrite is surfacing that fork rather than silently picking it. backlog is soft, same conditional catch-all role wrap-up-session's own entry described. consolidate-docs is soft: Step 6's rules-doc-size check recommends running it once a threshold's crossed, conditionally.

build.notes: The renamed design's own headline change: /build runs execution-gate automatically as its opening gate, unconditionally, with no approval question and no stated fallback - a genuinely hard edge now, where the pre-redesign equivalent (design-gate considering execution-gate) was explicitly optional. Step 4 invokes /verify unconditionally once implementation finishes - also hard. implement-queue is soft: batch mode is one of two mutually-exclusive entry paths (Step 0), and single-design mode - the common case - needs it not at all. local-delegate is soft: a Bucket A task flagged (local-delegate: implement) calls its runner script before drafting, but build is fully functional with the flag unset (the shipped default) or the component not installed at all - it just never fires.

verify.notes: code-reviewer is hard: Step 1 invokes it unconditionally, no fallback. ship is a soft pipeline-stage pointer to the natural next phase once QA passes - verify's own job ends at the QA gate record.

ship.notes: No dependency edges of its own kind: Step 1's publish-* dispatch is to an adopter's own tool-specific skill, never a component this export ships, and is fully conditional with an explicit stated fallback ('most work items have nothing to publish'). Step 2's archive-and-commit is functionally identical to what backlog/implement-queue already do for a no-deploy-target item - ship doesn't invoke either of them, they're alternate owners of the same step for different cases, stated explicitly in all three skills' own text rather than left to be inferred.

execution-gate.notes: Planning-phase skill - it recommends which bucket (main model / docs-writer / code-reviewer / fork) each task should use, it doesn't invoke them itself. Hard edge reflects that its output is meaningless without those agents existing to delegate to. Invoked automatically by build now (see build's own entry) rather than being invoked by spec at all.

external_prerequisites.name: Workflow tool with worktree support
external_prerequisites.note: D3 (build spec section 0): no reduced sequential mode is shipped. The skill and the process/workflows/implement-queue.js script both assume this is available; state the precondition in the README rather than building a second implementation.

implement-queue.notes: The .js workflow script (process/workflows/implement-queue.js) sets agentType: 'code-reviewer' / 'docs-writer' directly in its own agent() calls - confirmed by reading the built file, not inferred. spec/backlog are hard here because this skill's own checklist mechanism is meaningless without the upstream skills that populate and gate it. execution-gate is soft, not hard, for a corrected reason as of the two-axis redesign: it is no longer 'always optional' at all - build now runs it automatically and unconditionally - but implement-queue's own batch mode never invokes execution-gate directly itself; it only reads an already-filled execution-strategy section if one exists (written by build's automatic run, on a design implemented that way before reaching the queue) and works correctly without it. ship is soft: Step 5.4 dispatches archive-and-commit to it for a deploy-target item, conditionally, with an explicit stated fallback (do the archive move directly) for the no-deploy-target case.

external_prerequisites.degrades: the GPU pre-check treats a missing/erroring/timing-out nvidia-smi as busy, so no attempt is made - permanently true on non-NVIDIA hardware, a deliberate accepted tradeoff for a silent, safe-by-default feature

local-delegate.notes: No hard dependency on any other component - a standalone script + README that build calls into conditionally. build gains a soft edge to this component (see build's own entry); no other skill references it.

wrap-up-session.notes: Absorbed into end-task 2026-09-06 (next-command-contract redesign) as its full-sync depth mode. Now a 5-line redirect stub kept one cycle for backward compatibility - its own text points at end-task, no other functional dependency remains.

commit.notes: Absorbed into end-task 2026-09-06 (next-command-contract redesign) as its narrow-commit depth mode. Now a 5-line redirect stub kept one cycle for backward compatibility - its own text points at end-task, no other functional dependency remains.

handoff.notes: context-usage-nudge is standalone-shelf, not process-shelf - this is the one real process-to-standalone soft edge in the export. The skill's own text: 'if you have one wired up' - fully functional without it, just loses the automatic trigger. end-task is a contrast/naming reference only (2026-09-06 next-command-contract redesign renamed the skill this one isn't - previously wrap-up-session), same 'no functional call' relationship commit had with wrap-up-session before the absorption.
